item.vignette: A 13-year-old girl is evaluated after several episodes of carpopedal spasm. She has short stature, obesity, a round face, and shortened fourth metacarpals. Laboratory studies show low serum calcium, high serum phosphate, and markedly elevated parathyroid hormone despite normal renal function. Her mother has similar skeletal features and required calcium treatment during adolescence. Genetic testing identifies an inactivating variant in GNAS inherited from her mother.
item.lead_in: Which cellular signaling abnormality most directly explains this patient's biochemical findings?

options.A: Constitutive activation of the calcium-sensing receptor in parathyroid chief cells
options.B: Failure of parathyroid chief cells to synthesize parathyroid hormone
options.C: Reduced Gs-alpha stimulation of adenylate cyclase after parathyroid hormone receptor activation
options.D: Constitutive activation of the parathyroid hormone receptor in renal tubular cells
options.E: Reduced vitamin D receptor binding to DNA in intestinal epithelial cells

item.tested_construct: GNAS-mediated PTH resistance in pseudohypoparathyroidism type Ia

explanation.key_explanation: A maternally inherited inactivating GNAS variant can cause Albright hereditary osteodystrophy with PTH resistance. Reduced Gs-alpha signaling blunts adenylate cyclase/cAMP responses downstream of the PTH receptor, so PTH rises while calcium remains low and phosphate remains high.

distractor_explanations.A: Activating CaSR variants suppress PTH and cause hypocalcemia with inappropriately low PTH, not high PTH resistance.
distractor_explanations.B: The measured PTH is markedly elevated, excluding failed PTH synthesis.
distractor_explanations.C: Correct; GNAS encodes stimulatory G-protein signaling that couples receptors to adenylate cyclase.
distractor_explanations.D: Constitutive PTH-receptor activity would increase phosphate excretion and does not produce this resistance phenotype.
distractor_explanations.E: Vitamin D receptor dysfunction is a distinct disorder and does not explain the GNAS/Albright phenotype.

explanation.educational_objective: Recognize maternally inherited GNAS loss as impaired Gs-alpha/adenylate-cyclase signaling causing Albright hereditary osteodystrophy with PTH resistance.

evidence_map.claim: GNAS participates in stimulatory G-protein signaling to adenylate cyclase; maternal inactivating variants can produce AHO with hormone resistance.
evidence_map.item_specific_application: Explains high PTH with hypocalcemia/hyperphosphatemia and Albright features.

evidence_map.claim: CaSR activation suppresses PTH release.
Pseudohypoparathyroidism is PTH resistance rather than absent PTH production.
The documented GNAS defect reduces downstream signaling rather than constitutively activating PTHR.
The phenotype and maternal GNAS finding support G-protein hormone resistance rather than VDR dysfunction.

sources.supporting_passage: GNAS is part of stimulatory G-protein signaling to adenylate cyclase; maternal inactivating variants can produce AHO with multiple-hormone resistance.

item.vignette: A 2-week-old boy has recurrent lethargy and seizures. During an episode, plasma glucose is 28 mg/dL, insulin is inappropriately detectable, beta-hydroxybutyrate is very low, and free fatty acids are suppressed. Genetic testing identifies a biallelic loss-of-function variant in ABCC8, which encodes a subunit of the pancreatic beta-cell ATP-sensitive potassium channel.
item.lead_in: Which sequence of events most directly causes this infant's hypoglycemia?

options.A: Reduced KATP-channel activity → persistent beta-cell depolarization → voltage-gated calcium-channel opening → insulin release
options.B: Failure of KATP channels to close → beta-cell hyperpolarization → reduced calcium entry → insulin release
options.C: Reduced glucokinase activity → impaired glucose sensing → excessive insulin release at low glucose
options.D: Increased KATP-channel opening → membrane hyperpolarization → increased insulin granule exocytosis
options.E: Reduced insulin-receptor signaling in peripheral tissues → increased insulin secretion despite fasting

explanation.key_explanation: ABCC8 loss can reduce or abolish beta-cell KATP-channel activity. Persistent depolarization opens voltage-gated calcium channels and drives insulin granule exocytosis even when glucose is low.

distractor_explanations.A: Correct; reduced KATP activity causes persistent depolarization, calcium influx, and inappropriate insulin secretion.
distractor_explanations.B: KATP channels that fail to close reduce insulin secretion and are associated with neonatal diabetes.
distractor_explanations.C: Reduced glucokinase activity raises the glucose threshold for insulin release and causes GCK-MODY hyperglycemia.
distractor_explanations.D: KATP opening hyperpolarizes beta cells and suppresses calcium-dependent insulin release.
distractor_explanations.E: Peripheral insulin resistance does not explain severe neonatal hypoketotic hypoglycemia from ABCC8 loss.

explanation.educational_objective: Trace congenital hyperinsulinism from loss of beta-cell KATP-channel activity to depolarization, calcium influx, and inappropriate insulin secretion.

evidence_map.claim: ABCC8 encodes a KATP-channel subunit; reduced KATP activity drives inappropriate insulin secretion.
evidence_map.item_specific_application: Explains hypoketotic hypoglycemia with detectable insulin.

evidence_map.claim: KATP channels that do not close appropriately reduce insulin secretion and can cause neonatal diabetes.
Reduced GCK activity impairs glucose sensing and causes mild hyperglycemia.
KATP opening hyperpolarizes beta cells rather than triggering calcium-dependent insulin release.
ABCC8-associated congenital hyperinsulinism is a beta-cell secretion disorder rather than primary peripheral insulin resistance.

item.vignette: A 19-year-old woman is found to have a fasting plasma glucose of 124 mg/dL during a routine examination. Prior records show fasting glucose values between 112 and 128 mg/dL since childhood. She has never had ketoacidosis or symptomatic hyperglycemia. Her father and paternal grandmother have similarly mild, stable fasting hyperglycemia. Islet autoantibodies are negative. Genetic testing identifies a heterozygous loss-of-function variant in GCK.
item.lead_in: Which physiologic change most directly accounts for this patient's persistent mild hyperglycemia?

options.A: Increased hepatic gluconeogenesis due to constitutive glucagon-receptor signaling
options.B: Failure of pancreatic KATP channels to close despite rising intracellular ATP
options.C: Progressive autoimmune destruction of pancreatic beta cells
options.D: Increased insulin-receptor signaling in skeletal muscle
options.E: A higher glucose concentration is required for beta cells to sense glucose and trigger appropriate insulin secretion

item.tested_construct: Glucokinase as beta-cell glucose sensor in GCK-MODY

explanation.key_explanation: Glucokinase functions as a glucose sensor in pancreatic beta cells. Heterozygous loss of GCK activity shifts the threshold for glucose-stimulated insulin secretion upward, producing lifelong mild stable fasting hyperglycemia.

distractor_explanations.A: Constitutive glucagon signaling is not the inherited defect in GCK-MODY.
distractor_explanations.B: Failure of KATP closure is a different monogenic mechanism and typically produces neonatal diabetes.
distractor_explanations.C: Autoimmune beta-cell destruction is inconsistent with the stable multigenerational phenotype and negative antibodies.
distractor_explanations.D: Increased insulin-receptor signaling would lower plasma glucose.
distractor_explanations.E: Correct; reduced glucokinase activity shifts glucose-stimulated insulin secretion to a higher set point.

explanation.educational_objective: Recognize glucokinase as a beta-cell glucose sensor and GCK-MODY as an upward shift in the glucose threshold for insulin secretion.

evidence_map.claim: Glucokinase acts as a beta-cell glucose sensor; GCK loss reduces glucose sensing and insulin release.
evidence_map.item_specific_application: Explains lifelong mild stable fasting hyperglycemia.

evidence_map.claim: KATP channels that fail to close can cause neonatal diabetes with reduced insulin secretion.
MODY is monogenic beta-cell dysfunction rather than autoimmune destruction.
evidence_map.item_specific_application: Negative antibodies and family pattern support MODY.

evidence_map.claim: GCK-MODY is caused by reduced glucokinase activity rather than constitutive glucagon signaling.
The lesion impairs glucose sensing rather than increasing peripheral insulin signaling.

item.vignette: A 4-year-old boy has recurrent fasting hypoglycemia, poor weight gain, and progressive diffuse hyperpigmentation. Serum cortisol is very low and plasma ACTH is markedly elevated. Serum sodium and potassium are normal. Genetic testing identifies a biallelic pathogenic variant in MC2R. His adrenal glands are structurally normal on imaging.
item.lead_in: Which molecular defect most directly explains this patient's low cortisol concentration?

options.A: Constitutive activation of the mineralocorticoid receptor in the distal nephron
options.B: Failure of the adrenal ACTH receptor to reach the cell surface or bind ACTH effectively
options.C: Loss of 21-hydroxylase activity with accumulation of 17-hydroxyprogesterone
options.D: Constitutive activation of the glucocorticoid receptor in peripheral tissues
options.E: Failure of the pituitary corticotroph to synthesize ACTH

explanation.key_explanation: MC2R encodes the adrenal ACTH receptor. Pathogenic MC2R variants can prevent proper receptor trafficking or ACTH binding, producing ACTH resistance and low cortisol despite markedly elevated ACTH.

distractor_explanations.A: Mineralocorticoid-receptor activation does not explain isolated severe cortisol deficiency with high ACTH.
distractor_explanations.B: Correct; MC2R variants can impair receptor trafficking or ligand binding and block ACTH-driven glucocorticoid synthesis.
distractor_explanations.C: 21-hydroxylase deficiency is a steroidogenic enzyme defect, not the documented MC2R receptor defect.
distractor_explanations.D: Peripheral glucocorticoid-receptor activation does not block adrenal ACTH signaling.
distractor_explanations.E: Pituitary ACTH failure would produce low or inappropriately normal ACTH, not marked elevation.

explanation.educational_objective: Recognize familial glucocorticoid deficiency due to MC2R as ACTH resistance caused by defective adrenal ACTH-receptor trafficking or ligand binding.

evidence_map.claim: MC2R encodes the adrenal ACTH receptor; variants can impair surface trafficking or ACTH binding and block glucocorticoid production.
evidence_map.item_specific_application: Explains low cortisol despite very high ACTH.

evidence_map.claim: Familial glucocorticoid deficiency is adrenal unresponsiveness to ACTH rather than pituitary failure.
The documented MC2R variant identifies an ACTH-receptor signaling disorder rather than a steroidogenic enzyme defect.
MC2R affects ACTH-triggered glucocorticoid production, not distal-nephron mineralocorticoid signaling.
The causal defect is adrenal ACTH-receptor function rather than constitutive peripheral glucocorticoid-receptor activation.
evidence_map.item_specific_application: Does not explain high ACTH with low cortisol.

sources.title: MC2R gene: MedlinePlus Genetics
sources.supporting_passage: MC2R encodes the ACTH receptor; variants may prevent receptor transport to the membrane or ACTH binding, blocking glucocorticoid production.

sources.title: Familial glucocorticoid deficiency: MedlinePlus Genetics
sources.supporting_passage: Familial glucocorticoid deficiency causes hypoglycemia and hyperpigmentation; MC2R variants produce adrenal unresponsiveness to ACTH.

item.vignette: A 31-year-old woman is referred for persistent mild hypercalcemia discovered on routine testing. She feels well. Serum parathyroid hormone is in the upper-normal range despite the elevated calcium concentration. Twenty-four-hour urinary calcium excretion is low. Her father and two siblings have similar laboratory findings without nephrolithiasis. Genetic testing identifies a heterozygous loss-of-function variant in CASR.
item.lead_in: Which physiologic change most directly explains this patient's findings?

options.A: Increased sensitivity of parathyroid cells to extracellular calcium, causing excessive suppression of PTH
options.B: Increased renal calcium excretion due to exaggerated calcium-sensing receptor signaling
options.C: Autonomous PTH secretion from a monoclonal parathyroid adenoma
options.D: Reduced sensitivity of parathyroid and renal cells to extracellular calcium, shifting calcium feedback to a higher set point
options.E: Reduced intestinal calcium absorption due to impaired vitamin D receptor signaling

item.tested_construct: Familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia due to loss of CaSR function

explanation.key_explanation: Loss-of-function CASR variants reduce cellular sensitivity to extracellular calcium. Parathyroid cells require a higher calcium concentration to suppress PTH, while renal CaSR dysfunction favors calcium conservation and hypocalciuria.

distractor_explanations.A: Increased CaSR sensitivity causes autosomal dominant hypocalcemia by suppressing PTH at abnormally low calcium levels.
distractor_explanations.B: Exaggerated renal CaSR signaling decreases calcium reabsorption and promotes urinary calcium loss.
distractor_explanations.C: Adenoma-related primary hyperparathyroidism does not explain the inherited CASR variant with multigenerational hypocalciuria.
distractor_explanations.D: Correct; reduced CaSR function raises the calcium set point for PTH suppression and renal calcium excretion.
distractor_explanations.E: Impaired vitamin D signaling tends to reduce calcium absorption and does not explain familial hypercalcemia with hypocalciuria.

explanation.educational_objective: Recognize familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia as reduced CaSR sensitivity that raises the PTH suppression set point and increases renal calcium conservation.

evidence_map.claim: Loss of CaSR function reduces sensitivity to extracellular calcium and causes familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia.
evidence_map.item_specific_application: Explains mild hypercalcemia, non-suppressed PTH, hypocalciuria, and family history.

evidence_map.claim: Increased CaSR sensitivity suppresses PTH and causes autosomal dominant hypocalcemia.
Renal CaSR activation inhibits calcium reabsorption and increases urinary calcium.
The identified CASR loss-of-function variant and familial hypocalciuria support altered calcium sensing rather than acquired adenoma.
evidence_map.item_specific_application: Genetic and urinary pattern discriminate FHH.

evidence_map.claim: The causal lesion is CaSR-mediated calcium sensing rather than VDR signaling.

sources.supporting_passage: CaSR suppresses PTH and limits renal calcium reabsorption when calcium is high; loss of function can cause familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia, whereas gain of function causes hypocalcemia.
